newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Lower House approves MOF reform bill.
newsitem.headline: Japan Lower House approves MOF reform bill.

text.p: Japan's Lower House of parliament on Thursday approved a bill to set up a government inspection agency to oversee the financial sector, a move to reform the country's powerful Ministry of Finance (MOF).

The bill now passes to the Upper House for debate and is expected to become law by the end of the current parliament session in mid June, parliamentary officials said. The measures are due to go into effect next fiscal year.
The ministry, long viewed as the pinnacle of Japan's elite bureaucracy, has come under fire for its handling of the nation's banking woes and the secretive manner in which it deals with crises.
MOF and the Bank of Japan have also been under attack recently for failing to ferret out racketeer scandals at banks and brokerages during routine inspections.
The main points of the bill are as follows:
-- A fully independent body will be established under the Prime Minister's Office to take over MOF's functions of inspecting and supervising financial institutions.

-- The ministry's banking and securities bureaux will merge and take over some of the functions of the international finance bureau, although the international finance bureau will retain its basic structure for the time being.

-- The new body will oversee all financial institutions, including banks, agricultural financial firms, non-bank financial firms and labour credit associations, which are now supervised by various ministries.

-- The new body's inspection and supervisory functions will be shared with the Agriculture Ministry, the Labour Ministry and the Trade Ministry, which currently oversee certain financial institutions.
-- The new body must hold regular meetings with MOF to discuss financial matters from the viewpoint of maintaining order in Japan's credit markets.

-- The new agency will be responsible for handling financial failures but will be expected to consult the finance minister on any failures that could not be handled within the current framework. Severe crises will be dealt with by the cabinet and the agency.
-- The new agency will have jurisdiction over Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission.
-- MOF's regional bureaux will retain a role in the inspection and supervision of regional financial institutions.
